newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ASM Int sees recovery in second half of 97.
newsitem.headline: ASM Int sees recovery in second half of 97.

text.p: ASM International NV (ASMI) said on Monday it expects a recovery in the semiconductors market during the second half of 1997.
"We are now somewhere at the bottom of the cycle, which we expect to pick up somewhere in the second half of 1997," chief executive officer Arthur del Prado told reporters.
Del Prado was addressing journalists after ASMI announced that its earnings for the fourth quarter of 1996 and first two quarters of 1997 would be "substantially below" year-ago levels.

Del Prado declined to further specify the extent of the drop in earnings and also declined to give a forecast beyond the first half of 1997, saying it was very difficult to pinpoint exactly when the industry would start to pick up again.
In the longer term Del Prado said ASMI expected to grow at a faster rate than the semiconductor industry as a whole.

The "front-end" semiconductors business of wafer-processing was growing at a rate of 17-20 percent per year, while the "back-end" business of assembly and encapsulation was growing at around 15 percent a year, he said.
